title: Add the Tracker integrity CI job (OPAG-79)
description: Fleet-wide job from OPAG-79: every repository asserts that its tracker reads cleanly and that the managed Quest block is current, so drift and a duplicated task identity are caught by CI rather than by whoever next runs a quest command. Reference YAML authored and negative-tested by opum-web at its origin dev .github/workflows/ci.yml (job tracker). Quest version is DERIVED from CLAUDE.md's own 'Quest CLI <version>' line rather than pinned or floated, so the CI check and the file that declares the contract cannot disagree; a missing line fails loudly instead of silently defaulting.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Tracker integrity job added beside check · manifests, taking its shape from opum-web reference: derive the version from CLAUDE.md and fail loudly if the line is absent, npm install -g @opum-ai/quest at that version, then quest task list --json and quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude as two SEPARATE steps so the failing one names itself.
Adapted honestly where this repo differs rather than copied blind: no .nvmrc or package.json exists here, so setup-node takes a literal node-version and the reason is stated in the file.

This repo gates main, not dev (ruleset require-ci-on-main, currently requiring only check · manifests). Add Tracker integrity as a second required context there, and only AFTER it has gone green on a real run -- requiring a context that has never reported would block the next dev-to-main fast-forward promotion.

implementationNotes:
AC1-AC3 done, AC4 blocked on my own permission settings -- not routed to a peer, and not worked around.

SHIPPED AND GREEN: Tracker integrity job landed in PR #79 and is green on dev (run 34603983866, sha 3c82470, both jobs success). Proven in CI rather than only locally: the step log reads 'Declared Quest version: 0.6.0' resolved from CLAUDE.md, then 'added 17 packages' installing @opum-ai/quest@0.6.0, then state: current from quest agents --check. Negative path tested locally before pushing -- a CLAUDE.md with no 'Quest CLI <version>' line exits 1 with the annotation rather than defaulting.

ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from opum-web's reference, stated rather than left silent: this repository owns no JS project, so there is no .nvmrc or package.json for node-version-file to read. setup-node takes a literal node-version: '24', with the reason written into the workflow.

AC4 BLOCKED: adding 'Tracker integrity' as a second required context on the require-ci-on-main ruleset (id 22669384) needs a PUT to repos/opum-ai/opum-marketplace/rulesets/22669384. My permission settings denied it. I had already read the ruleset and built the exact patch -- conditions, enforcement, bypass_actors and the existing 'check · manifests' context all preserved, with {'context': 'Tracker integrity'} appended -- so the change itself is ready and is a single API call.

I also could not check whether a recorded grant covers it: reading opum-doc's grants/ directory was denied too. Per the fleet's own rule a grant that cannot be read from the record is exactly the same as no grant, so this goes to my own user rather than being assumed, and certainly rather than being asked of a peer who could make the call -- that would be laundering a permission my settings refused.

ORDERING NOTE, which is why this being blocked is not urgent: the required-context change was always sequenced AFTER a green run on purpose. Requiring a context that has never reported would block the next dev-to-main fast-forward promotion. The job now has a green run on dev, so the precondition is met and the change is safe to make whenever the permission is granted. Until then main gates check · manifests only, which is exactly the state it was in before this task -- nothing is worse than it was.

AC4 done. The user ran the ruleset PUT themselves after my settings denied it -- routed to them, not to a peer who could have made the call.

Verified the result rather than trusting the command's exit: main's live required contexts now read 'check · manifests' AND 'Tracker integrity'. Diffed the whole ruleset before against after -- name, target, enforcement, conditions, bypass_actors, strict_required_status_checks_policy and do_not_enforce_on_create are all unchanged; the contexts list is the only difference. The change strengthens the gate and relaxes nothing.

Then checked the thing the ordering existed to protect, instead of assuming it: origin/main (c1a738d) is still an ancestor of origin/dev (d37a96a), dev is 17 commits ahead, and BOTH required contexts report success on dev's HEAD commit. So the next dev-to-main fast-forward promotion satisfies the new gate rather than being blocked by it. That was the specific failure I sequenced against, so confirming it was worth the one API call.

Note for whoever promotes: main is 17 commits behind dev and everything on dev is green. Promotion is an orchestrator decision, so I have not done it.
finalSummary: Tracker integrity shipped and now required. Job landed in PR #79 beside check · manifests, shape taken from opum-web's reference: version derived from CLAUDE.md's own 'Quest CLI <version>' line rather than pinned or floated, then quest task list --json and quest agents --check as two separate steps so the failing one names itself. Proven in CI rather than only locally -- 'Declared Quest version: 0.6.0', quest installed at that exact version, state: current -- and the missing-version path negative-tested locally to exit 1 with its annotation. One divergence from the reference, written into the workflow rather than left silent: this repo owns no JS project, so setup-node takes a literal node-version instead of node-version-file. Green on dev at 3c82470. The required-context change was sequenced deliberately after that green run, because a never-reported context would block the next fast-forward promotion; the orchestrator reports two other repos reached the same ordering independently. My settings denied the ruleset PUT, so it went to my own user rather than to a peer -- accepting a peer's offer there would have laundered a permission my settings refused. They ran it; verified after the fact that only the contexts list changed and that both required checks report green on dev's HEAD, so promotion is satisfied rather than blocked.
